findings.text: `task_for()` in Server/health.mjs only looks for the editing task's `task.jsonl` under today's and yesterday's `ai/` day folder (the fallback branch after the "file lives inside a task dir" check). A file edited by a multi-day/foundational task (dated, say, `ai/2026-09-25/…/`, which CLAUDE.md explicitly says never gets capped or rushed) will never match, so its health findings silently fall through to the health day log instead of landing on that task's card — exactly the report-to-the-dashboard behavior item 10/3 asks for. The tradeoff is a deliberate, documented decision (monitor/task.jsonl, "which-task": scanning all of `public/` was rejected as "too slow"), but scanning every *unlanded* `task.jsonl` under `ai/` (a small set at any time, not all of `public/`) would be cheap and correct without the two-day blind spot.

Proofs 1–3 on the card each link a concrete artifact (a shot, a task-log excerpt, a console log). Proof 4, "one supervisor" (health-supervisor.mjs's per-tree pid lock), has no attached log or screenshot — only the claim in `monitor/task.jsonl` line 8 ("two started 4 s apart… second exited code 0"). Worth asking for the console output of that run before counting it proven.

`note_skipped()` (Server/health.mjs, the "data only, no check" console line) uses one shared debounce timer that keeps getting reset on every new skipped file. If data-file writes keep arriving under 1.5 s apart — plausible on a busy day with many agents appending JSONL — the summary line never prints, even though no checks are being lost. Cosmetic only, but it means that console signal can't always be trusted to confirm "nothing was checked."

`check_one()`'s settle-probe (`within(probe, …)`) runs regardless of whether `page.goto()` already failed, and on a genuinely hung page `goto`'s own 15 s timeout can eat most of the 10 s `SETTLE_MS` budget before the probe even starts, so a slow-but-not-stalled page could be reported as "still busy" instead of its real navigation error. In practice this looks safe today because `context.routeWebSocket` already closes sockets that would otherwise block `networkidle`, so a real-world false positive is unlikely — flagging only because the two timeouts (goto's 15 s, settle's 10 s measured from the same start) aren't coordinated, and the original nav error gets discarded rather than reported alongside the stall finding.

Item 12(b) is not in the diff. `public/framework/ext/JSONL/JSONL.js` on `worktree/proposal-flow` still lacks `experiment` and `review`, and it still warns on flat lines. The verbs-reader work exists only as an uncommitted edit in the worktree (`git status`: ` M public/framework/ext/JSONL/JSONL.js`), so `/framework/ai2/` keeps printing `JSONL: unknown verb` until that edit is committed and merged.

When that JSONL.js lands, drop `experiment` and `review` from `pending` in `.claude/hooks/jsonl-schema.mjs:43`. The test (`jsonl-schema.test.mjs`) only prints a "note" when this is stale, so it will not catch the drift; make that note fail the test instead.
Don't merge the worktree's other ~230 uncommitted `files.jsonl` changes (`public/files.jsonl`, `ai/2026-08-*/…/files.jsonl`) along with item 1. They look like regenerated data, not this task's work.

Items 1–7 (Proposal class, node-led loop, Inbox, weights, the architect's §6 list, the UI feedback loop) are not in this diff. `plan.md` defers them to wave B, which matches the owner's "do these first", so this review covers wave A (items 8–12) only.

Item 8 asked for "a cheap anomaly check" (the 8×38 stretched unread dot). Nothing in `Server/health.mjs` would catch that; only the old spacing lints run. Item 10 says "a layout scan comes later", so this is fine if it is deliberate, but say so on the card.

The stall reading in `Server/health.mjs` (check_one, around diff line 552) comes after `setViewportSize(1920×1080)`. The relayout from that resize is the watcher's own work, and on a heavy page it could count as the page's long task. Reading `__health_longtasks` before the resize would avoid that.

`report_to_dashboard()` writes one `log` line per checked page into the editor's task.jsonl, so a change to a shared module (up to 8 pages) puts 8 health lines on that card per edit. One summary line per batch would be easier for the owner to read.

The earlier review's [fix] (finding tasks only from the last two days) is resolved. `task_for()` now falls back to scanning every task under `ai/` with an mtime cache, and `monitor/proof/task-lookup.log` proves it.

`.md` changes no longer trigger a check (`TEMPLATE_RE` in `Server/health.mjs`). A readme or `doc/*.md` is rendered by a page's Docs tab, so a broken one goes unseen. This follows the owner's "template, not data" words, but it is worth a line in `Server/doc/health.md`.

`.claude/hooks/jsonl-guard.mjs` reads command text, so `Set-Content out.txt (Get-Content a.jsonl)` or a commit message quoting `>> x.jsonl` is blocked by mistake. The readme names the second case; this is acceptable because the guard fails open on its own errors and points to the right tool.

`JSONL.apply()` is now lenient in two ways that could change state without any warning. (a) A line with no verb that has an `at` and nothing to read is merged with `assign`, so a stray `{"at":…,"title":"x"}` would silently rename the task. (b) A single verb with stray keys folds them into the verb's value, and a string value becomes `{…stray, msg}`, which a handler expecting a string (`agent`, `ask`) may not understand. The validator now refuses both shapes on write, so the risk is limited to old lines. It is still worth one demo or test line each.

Items 1–7 (the Proposal class, the node-led loop, the Inbox, impact weights, the architect's §6 list, the phased UI loop) are not in this diff. [plan.md](../plan.md) defers them to wave B, which matches the owner's "DO THESE FIRST". This review covers wave A only.
